short_en: Yes. Struggling with doubts is not the same as rejecting the faith. The Church separates doubts that come to you from doubt you choose and feed. Bring your questions to God, like the father in the Gospel: "I believe; help my unbelief!"
short_ar: نعم. أن تصارع الشكوك ليس كأن ترفض الإيمان. الكنيسة تميّز بين شكٍّ يأتيك رغماً عنك، وشكٍّ تختاره وتغذّيه. احمل أسئلتك إلى الله، مثل الأب في الإنجيل: "أؤمن يا سيّد، فأعِن عدم إيماني!"
share_en: Having questions doesn't make you an unbeliever. Bring them to God, and keep walking.
share_ar: أن تكون عندك أسئلة لا يجعلك غير مؤمن. احملها إلى الله… وتابِع الطريق.
anim: A young woman walks through a dark tunnel holding a small lamp marked "faith"; question marks float around her, but each step lights the next stone, until light appears at the end.

en.story:
For nearly 50 years, Mother Teresa of Calcutta felt no sense of God's presence. More than 40 of her letters, published in 2007 as Come Be My Light (she had asked for them to be destroyed), speak of dryness, darkness and loneliness; two of them even voice doubt that God exists. Yet she kept rising at 4:30 every morning and kept serving the poorest of Kolkata. She never gave up her faith or her work. In 2016 the Church declared her a saint. (TIME, 2007)

Honest note: her darkness was mostly a felt absence of God, what spiritual writers call a "dark night," more than an intellectual rejection of the faith.
en.deeper: The Catechism makes a clear distinction. Involuntary doubt (hesitation, trouble answering objections, anxiety because faith is obscure) happens to believers. Voluntary doubt means deciding to treat what God revealed as false or uncertain; cultivated on purpose, it can lead to spiritual blindness (CCC 2088). As St John Henry Newman put it: "Ten thousand difficulties do not make one doubt" (CCC 157). Faith is often lived in darkness and can be tested (CCC 164). This whole course was written partly to strengthen believers who harbour doubts (SoA God, Introduction, p. 8). When doubt is more emotional than intellectual, the course suggests acting as a believer (praying, going to Mass) and letting the heart follow, as Pascal and C.S. Lewis advised (SoA God L47, pp. 144–145). Questions are welcome; what matters is asking them honestly, and asking God too.
en.proof:
• Her letters are real and public: more than 40 of them, many never published before 2007, describe the darkness of her last half-century. (TIME, 2007)
  • The Church knew, and still called her holy: at her beatification on 19 October 2003, St John Paul II spoke openly of her long years of "inner darkness" (homily, vatican.va); Pope Francis canonized her on 4 September 2016 (homily, vatican.va).
en.bible:
• "I believe; help my unbelief!" — Mk 9:24
  • "O man of little faith, why did you doubt?" (said as Jesus catches Peter's hand) — Mt 14:31
  • "They worshiped him; but some doubted." — Mt 28:17
  • CCC 157, 164, 2088
